Forensic Cash Quality & Balance Sheet Fortress Assessment

Aeva operates a capital-light, fabless manufacturing strategy leveraging contract foundries for its silicon photonics engine, resulting in $0.00M CapEx for Q3 2026. Reported FCF is -$30.37M. Adjusting for non-cash stock compensation of $11.41M, True Economic FCF burn stands at $-41.78M.

• Available Liquidity Runway: Available liquidity of $272.5M provides over 24 months of operational runway at current net burn rates, fully bridging the gap to 2027 OEM series production revenue ramps.
• Zero Long-Term Debt: Aeva carries zero debt obligations on its balance sheet, eliminating structural interest rate burdens, refinancing maturities, or covenants.
• SBC Non-Cash Impact: Non-cash stock-based compensation of $11.41M represents competitive equity retention for elite photonics and software engineers while conserving vital cash reserves.
• Working Capital Inflows: Inventories and pre-payments stabilized at $24.8M as raw wafer procurement transitioned into staged supplier commitments ahead of factory automation deployments.
Row 4: Operational Wins, Drags & Earnings Call Q&A Audit
QUALITATIVE & TRANSCRIPT FORENSICS

Operational Wins & Catalysts

  • Micro-Epsilon Supply Agreement: Secured multi-year contract for precision industrial sensing with initial multi-thousand sensor order received.
  • US Defense Selection: Selected by US Air Force and US Navy to develop airborne autonomy capabilities utilizing FMCW velocity sensing.
  • AI Optical Connectivity: Announced ultra-high-power optical source modules for AI data center optical transceivers, tapping hyperscaler demand.
  • Daimler Truck Progress: Maintained on-schedule execution toward 2027 commercial Class 8 autonomous series production.

Execution Drags & Watch Items

  • Revenue Timing Slip: Q3 revenue of $6.67M came in slightly below the $6.80M Street consensus due to customer shipment staging into Q4.
  • Elevated Cash Burn: Quarterly operating cash burn of -$30.37M continues while waiting for high-volume series production to ramp in 2027.
  • Stock Compensation Rise: SBC climbed to $11.41M in Q3, increasing from $8.51M in the prior quarter as engineering talent is retained.
  • Automotive Customer Lead Times: Passenger vehicle and trucking validation cycles remain multi-year, requiring disciplined liquidity management.

Top Institutional Analyst Q&A and Analyst Questions Forensic Exchanges

Colin Langan (Wells Fargo) Micro-Epsilon Multi-Year Commercial Supply Agreement & Unit Volumes

Question: Soroush, the Micro-Epsilon contract win mentions an initial multi-thousand sensor order. How should we think about the revenue ramp from factory automation relative to automotive?

Executive Answer: Soroush Salehian (CEO) answered: 'Micro-Epsilon is a global leader in precision industrial sensors. The multi-thousand unit order represents immediate commercial monetization of our FMCW technology with ASPs and margins that exceed automotive sensor benchmarks. Shipments commence in Q4 2026 and will scale meaningfully throughout 2027.'

Tristan Gerra (Baird) Daimler Truck Series Production Milestones & Class 8 Commercial Readiness

Question: Can you provide an update on testing and verification milestones with Daimler Truck as you approach series production?

Executive Answer: Soroush Salehian stated: 'We continue to hit every scheduled technical gate with Daimler Truck. Our Atlas 4D LiDAR is currently undergoing winter validation and real-world highway track testing. Customer feedback on velocity per point in adverse weather continues to validate FMCW as the only technology capable of meeting heavy truck stopping distance requirements.'

Mark Delaney (Goldman Sachs) Optical Connectivity for AI Data Centers & Hyperscaler Engagements

Question: Soroush, you announced expansion into ultra-high-power optical sources for AI data center optical connectivity. What is the commercial pipeline and customer appetite?

Executive Answer: Soroush Salehian explained: 'Next-generation AI clusters require high-power continuous wave optical sources for co-packaged optics and optical transceivers. Because our FMCW LiDAR engine is built on high-power silicon photonics laser arrays, we can repurpose this technology directly into AI data center connectivity. Customer engagement with major hyperscalers is accelerating rapidly.'

Suji Desilva (ROTH Capital Partners) SICK Industrial Sensor Traction & Automotive Pipeline Conversion

Question: Can you elaborate on how the SICK partnership is progressing following their first Eve-powered sensor launch, and what are the gating factors for additional automotive OEM production awards?

Executive Answer: Soroush Salehian highlighted: 'SICK's launch has opened immediate conversations across factory automation and robotic logistics. Because Eve delivers millimeter precision velocity data, customers can deploy dynamic safety perimeters that conventional 3D LiDAR cannot match. For automotive OEMs, our joint development with Bendix is establishing the reference standard for commercial vehicle ADAS, and we expect further customer announcements over the coming two quarters.'

Microblogging & Desk Takeaway: Aeva delivered a solid commercial execution print for Q3 2026. Revenue of $6.67M surged +86.3% YoY, narrowly missing consensus ($6.80M) due to shipment timing, while gross margin expanded to 33.58%. Crucially, Aeva announced multi-market commercial breakthroughs: a multi-year industrial supply deal with Micro-Epsilon (initial multi-thousand sensor order), US Air Force/Navy defense contracts, and expansion into AI optical connectivity modules. Forward Q4 revenue guidance of $7.3M-$8.3M ($7.8M midpoint) was raised above Street consensus ($7.50M), while available liquidity of $272.5M secures runway into 2028.
